scope: Historical male sovereign source audit for the sixteen Event 012 Africa priority members.
runtime_policy: All files in this package are source evidence only. No file authorizes a GFX edit, gameplay wiring, identity substitution, or generated real-person portrait.

entries.candidate_identity: Prempeh I, with attendants; exact individual position in the group is not independently confirmed
entries.source_attribution: Richardis, University of Paris 1 image record, circa 1900
entries.license: Commons public-domain record; source provenance and exact group position still require review
entries.uncertainty: Prempeh II is already owned by Event 006; the Prempeh I group crop is evidence-only until the exact face is independently located. Do not clone Prempeh II or relabel the group crop.

entries.candidate_identity: Unnamed Alaafin of Oyo, mounted figure in an office-captioned image
entries.source_attribution: National Archives UK, Africa Through a Lens, record CO1069
entries.license: Open Government Licence v1.0 as recorded by Commons
entries.era_fit: period-compatible, but identity is not named
entries.uncertainty: The rider's face is obscured by a large hat or veil and the caption names only the office. It cannot safely stand for Lawani Agogoija, Siyanbola Ladigbolu, or another named Alaafin.

entries.candidate_identity: Sir Siddiq Abubakar III, Sultan of Sokoto
entries.source_attribution: Eliot Elisofon, Smithsonian National Museum of African Art / Photographic Archives
entries.license: Commons public-domain claim under Nigerian law, but Smithsonian metadata requests permission for reproducing the archive image
entries.era_fit: late-colonial/postwar; period-compatible only for a matching setting
entries.uncertainty: Permission and redistribution status must be cleared before any repaint or runtime use. Visible white turban, robe, blue embroidered cloak, and beads are source facts only.

entries.source_attribution: The Nigeria Handbook, 11th edition, West Africa Ltd.; vendor scan at https://www.antiquemapsandprints.com/categories/prints-and-maps-by-country/africa/nigeria/product/nigeria-the-shehu-of-bornu-1936-old-vintage-print-picture/P-6-031793~P-6-031793
entries.license: Public-domain work as recorded by Commons; selected byte is a vendor scan, not a direct Commons download
entries.current_runtime_status: promoted separately through the independently reviewed source-locked repaint; this evidence DDS is not the runtime file
entries.uncertainty: Retain the Commons and vendor provenance together. Do not add a sword, spear, mask, face paint, or insignia not visible in the source.

entries.era_fit: Manden Empire identity is primarily pre-photography
entries.uncertainty: No named, era-appropriate, defensible male photograph was found. Generic Mandinka imagery and modern reconstructions are not substitutes.

entries.source_attribution: Sociedade de Geografia de Lisboa collection
entries.current_runtime_status: promoted separately through the independently reviewed source-locked repaint; this evidence DDS is not the runtime file

entries.candidate_identity: Daudi Cwa II, Kabaka of Buganda
entries.source_attribution: Jules Leclercq, Aux sources du Nil, Plon-Nourrit, Paris, 1913
entries.license: Public Domain Mark 1.0; published 1913, author record not identified
entries.uncertainty: Exact named plate and crop are strong, but this is source evidence only; a source-locked repaint and independent likeness/style audit are still required. Preserve the visible throne, cap, robe, sash, and staff without additions.
Haile Selassie is a different twentieth-century Ethiopian identity and cannot silently substitute for an ancient Aksumite monarch.

entries.candidate_identity: Albert Kalonji, self-declared Mulopwe/Emperor of South Kasai
entries.source_attribution: Official portrait, photographer unknown; Commons metadata references AP News Library and a modern uploader
entries.license: Commons public-domain claim under Democratic Republic of the Congo law; uploader and AP provenance require review
entries.era_fit: postwar; compatible only with a matching alternate-history setting
entries.uncertainty: Do not promote until rights, provenance, and the requested Event 012 date/identity relationship are reviewed. The source visibly shows a crown, suit, and throne only.

entries.candidate_identity: Mwaantayaav Mbaku Citend, supreme ruler of Lunda
entries.source_attribution: Daniel P. Biebuyck, personal archive page naming the 1957 supreme ruler
entries.license: No reusable license granted on the source page; photographer permission required
entries.uncertainty: Permission is open. Preserve the photographed beaded jacket, raffia skirt, beaded hat, sheathed knife, bracelet, medal, and throne context; invent no additional regalia.

entries.era_fit: medieval Great Zimbabwe identity is pre-photography
